D2·ea2q — 2026-09-15
rule: Hot-path Rust code reproduces the JavaScript text semantics pinned in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins, never Rust defaults; a parity difference is fixed in Rust or ruled by a Decision, never absorbed by loosening the conformance suite.
chose: Byte parity is defined against the TypeScript engine's JavaScript text semantics, inventoried in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins: lengths and clips in UTF-16 code units, JS non-unicode regex classes, JS whitespace class, ECMAScript number formatting in canonical JSON, Node path.relative/basename, Math.round half-up, millisecond ISO timestamps. docs/HOTPATH.md is the hand-written contract inventory the conformance suite (1.2) drives; SPEC gaps it lists (G1–G15) are resolved by SPEC edits or Decisions, never by letting the two implementations differ.
over: Rust-native defaults (char/byte lengths, Unicode-aware regex classes, ryu number formatting) with SPEC amended to tolerate the drift between implementations.
because: The 10k injection cap, every clip budget, the redaction and guard regexes and the canonical event bytes all decide observable output; a Rust core that used its own defaults would pass no golden test against the live 9.4 MB record and would fork events.jsonl bytes on identical events (the spurious-diff hazard SPEC §Event envelope exists to prevent). Reproducing JS semantics is cheap and mechanical; tolerating drift would make "same bytes from both implementations" (D1) unprovable.
